overview: FAM4104 is a flight event focused on crosswind takeoff/approach/landing. The notes below are organized off the canonical syllabus items first, then filled out with local FAM gouge so students can brief the event, explain the why behind each item, and stay ahead of instructor follow-up questions.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion items

children.text: use crab and wing-low techniques to stay aligned with the runway in crosswind conditions. Adjust bank, power, and control inputs as needed; waveoff if overbanking is required
land into XW using wing-low method, touch down on upwind gear first; waveoff if side motion, drift, or crab occurs
Description:
Setup / entry
Procedures:
Recovery (Standard OCF/Incipient Spin):
Failure to reduce aileron as speed builds.
Improper rudder use leading to drift or weathervaning.
Skipping due to premature liftoff on upwind wing.
Pattern Adjustments for Crosswinds
crab into the wind to maintain correct WTD
Approach Turn:
Adjust bank and power to counter overshooting or undershooting
Final (Groove):
Wing-Low Method
Aileron into the wind - prevent drift
Max AOB 45°; waveoff if more is required
+½ gust factor to final approach speed (max +10 kts)
Use rudder/brakes to stay straight; brakes below 80 KIAS
PCL - MAX, rotate at 90 KIAS
Applying brakes before 80 KIAS.
Spin-like motions with oscillations; lasts about 2 turns; recover with inadvertent departure procedure.
Stable spin, 2-3 sec/turn, ~4500 ft altitude loss per 6 turns; neutral controls initially, then antispin inputs to recover.
Not rolling past 90° AOB
Monitor Airspeed - (≤316 KIAS), execute AGSM
If AOA <18 units and airspeed <110 KIAS, advance PCL
Common errors / grading traps
The usual trap is missing the setup picture, then trying to salvage Crosswind Takeoff/Approach/Landing late.
stick shaker/buffet = imminent stall - reduce back pressure
Warnings:
Description:
Improper/aggressive controls near stall, mechanical failure, atmospheric conditions, or combinations.
Aircraft moves unpredictably after stall; controls may feel ineffective or reversed.
OCF phases:
Uncommanded rapid motions, controls ineffective; neutral controls + idle power recommended.
PCL — IDLE
Controls — NEUTRAL
Altitude — CHECK
Failing to reduce power/deploy speed brake
Not reporting oil pressure
Inverted:
UA recovery does not work if stalled or in OCF
Common errors / grading traps
The common trap is memorizing isolated facts about Ocf without being able to explain the operational consequence.
Warnings:
recovery from NH, NL, or Inverted attitudes due to disorientation, misflown maneuvers, or external factors. Recovery is visual (VFR) and must be completed above 6000’ AGL
Nose-High:
PCL - MAX (if low airspeed)
Use back stick to bring nose to horizon
Roll upright as nose approaches horizon
Roll wings level, raise nose, check oil pressure, power as req.
Not setting PCL to MAX at low airspeed
Pushing forward stick (zero or -Gs)
Stopping roll with nose still above horizon
